title: Leadership
description: Who holds authority in Ide, and in what proportion.
html:
THE ROLES

The roles

RoleIdeWho holds itWhat it is
head of the polityIkalamanthe divine king-priest; chosen from Ono-Idenze
holy queenIyiwomanchosen through Ono-Akunnia. She holds LITTLE temporal power and is not a ruler: she is a superior, the supreme mother of the religion, as the supreme mother is venerated in Catholicism. Her authority is moral and maternal, not political
council of male eldersOmunnameninheritance, land rights, justice, ritual duty
council of female eldersOmuadawomenled by Isu Ada; marriage, childbirth, purity, moral order
council of the wiseNde Akomen and womenadvises the Ikala and executes royal policy
head of a clanIkakamanan Ichie-level chief over an uniku
the composition rule——leadership roles are mostly held by men, and women hold 35 percent of them (35% women.)

THE COMPOSITION RULE

Mostly men, and 35 percent women

Leadership is mostly held by men, and women hold 35 percent of it. The proportion is the rule, not a description: the Omuada and the Iyi are a council, not a token, and the composition of every body is measured against the 35 percent. The Omunna and the Omuada sit in every town, so balance in governance is a core Ide principle.
